report.source_text: The woman was given antituberculous medicine and was followed in an outpatient clinic. Her symptoms and indications improved noticeably over time. Her symptoms began to improve significantly; she began to gain weight and feel stronger.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Tuberculosis of mesenteric lymph nodes confirmed by PCR
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old woman presented with 2 months of abdominal pain, postprandial worsening, diarrhea, weight loss, and bloating. Labs showed anemia, leukocytosis, elevated ESR, and H. pylori infection. Abdominal CT revealed distended ileum, dilated small bowel loops, minimal free fluid near terminal ileum and inflammatory changes in cecum and ascending colon suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease. Mesenteric lymph node biopsies PCR confirmed M tuberculosis infection. She was treated with antituberculous medication with subsequent clinical improvement and weight gain.
